title: Modules, source loading and reproducible projects
outcome: Separate namespaces from source files, execute a tiny owned multi-file project offline, and distinguish locked dependencies from code loading.
key_terms: A separate global namespace declared with `module`, so names defined inside it do not collide with names elsewhere.
A declaration that makes selected module names available unqualified after `using`, while other names still need qualification.
A call that evaluates another source file in the current module as if its code were written there.
The environment file listing direct dependencies by name and UUID, along with compatibility bounds.
The environment file recording the exact resolved version of every direct and indirect dependency.
approach: Modules are namespaces, files are source text, and project files record dependencies; keep the three apart. `LocalStats.center` subtracts the mean and rejects empty input. Worked example B writes a tiny `TinyScale` project into a temporary directory and includes its test file into a fresh module with no network or package resolution.

exercises.title: Use qualified access
exercises.answer: Qualified access works even without bringing the export into the caller namespace.
exercises.why: The mean of `[2, 4]` is 3, so subtracting it gives `[-1, 1]`, reached through the module name `LocalStats`.
exercises.wrong: Calling `center` without qualification or `using .LocalStats` fails with `UndefVarError`, since the name lives inside the module.

exercises.title: Trace exports
exercises.task: Explain whether export makes other names private.
exercises.hint: Compare name lookup with access control.
exercises.answer: Export controls convenient importing; module qualification is not a security boundary.
exercises.why: `export center` only decides what `using` brings in; any unexported name is still reachable as `LocalStats.name`.
exercises.wrong: Leaving a helper unexported to hide a secret assumes access control that Julia modules do not provide.
exercises.verify: Check `:center in names(LocalStats)` and confirm an unexported helper is still callable with a qualified name.

exercises.title: Inspect the project fixture
exercises.task: Identify which file declares identity and which defines twice.
exercises.expected: Project.toml declares identity; src/TinyScale.jl defines behavior.
exercises.hint: The test file consumes the source.
exercises.answer: Metadata, implementation and tests serve distinct roles.
exercises.why: `Project.toml` holds the name, UUID and version, `src/TinyScale.jl` defines `twice`, and `test/runtests.jl` exercises it.
exercises.wrong: Putting test assertions in the source module makes every import run them and mixes behavior with verification.
exercises.verify: Example B asserts `isfile(joinpath(root, "Project.toml"))` and that including the tests returns `true`.

exercises.title: Debug relative paths
exercises.task: Explain why @__DIR__ is used in the test entrypoint.
exercises.expected: It anchors the path at the source file.
exercises.hint: The process working directory may differ.
exercises.answer: Source-relative paths avoid hidden dependence on where the command was launched.
exercises.why: `@__DIR__` expands to the directory of the file that contains it, so the path to `../src/TinyScale.jl` works from any working directory.
exercises.wrong: Writing `include("src/TinyScale.jl")` works only when the process starts in the project root.
exercises.verify: Run the test file from another directory and confirm it still loads; the reference shows a missing path raising `SystemError`.

exercises.title: Design reproducible dependencies
exercises.task: List what Project and Manifest do and do not establish.
exercises.expected: They identify declared and resolved dependency state.
exercises.hint: Hardware, data and external services need separate records.
exercises.answer: A lock graph supports reproduction but does not alone qualify scientific outputs or service availability.
exercises.why: A manifest records resolved package versions, which helps reproduce code, but it does not record hardware, data files or remote services.
exercises.wrong: Claiming a result is reproducible because a manifest is committed ignores changes in input data or BLAS threads.
exercises.verify: List the extra facts, such as data checksum and thread count, alongside the manifest.

exercises.title: Transfer into a real package
exercises.task: Separate a CSV workflow into numerical core, IO and tests.
exercises.expected: The core takes values and returns values without network calls.
exercises.hint: Keep side effects at explicit boundaries.
exercises.answer: A pure public kernel is independently testable; IO and package operations can have separate integration checks.
exercises.why: A pure function that takes a vector of numbers and returns results can be tested without files, while reading CSV stays in a thin IO layer.
exercises.wrong: Reading the file inside the numerical function forces every unit test to create files and couples failures in IO with math errors.
exercises.verify: Write one unit test that calls the core with literal values and one integration test that reads a small file.

checks_note: The module lines use qualified access and also confirm that `center` is listed among exported names. The final `SystemError` shows that a missing source path fails at include time instead of later, at first use. The `joinpath` comparison is a reminder that file paths and module names are different strings, so renaming one does not rename the other.
